newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPG lower to steady amid weak NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPG lower to steady amid weak NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot LPG prices were mostly lower in late trade on Monday, tracking falling NYMEX futures but still remaining at high price levels, traders said.
Dealings were light, however, as many people stood back to see how hard the NYMEX will fall and if tension between the U.S. and Iraq continue to slightly ease.

"The done deals were very few," said one Houston-based trader. "People are standing back with (NYMEX) coming off as hard as it did and many are leaning on the sell side with there being no military action in Iraq right now."

NYMEX October crude oil futures cratered just before the close on rumors the U.S. had asked Saudi Arabi to increase its oil production to compensate for the loss of Iraqi oil sales. U.S. and Mideast sources denied the report.
In the Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, propane remained between 47.00 cents to 47.25 cents a gallon, after dropping more than one cent at midday.
Conway, Kansas, hub material traded at 43.75 cents, 0.75 cents below midday levels.
Prices remained at higher than usual levels, however, due to low inventories, both primary and secondary, traders said.
-- Laney Salisbury New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
